name: Cave Pagoda
kicker: Hill pagoda on the slope of Núi Sam
summary: Chùa Hang, also called Phước Điền, is the climb on Núi Sam, not a flat hall at the foot. Vietnam Tourism says the view from the climb reaches toward Cambodia, and that caves run into the hillside if you have time. Hours, a fee, and a fixed length were not printed. Check on arrival. Go when the air is clear if the plain is the point.
getThere: Continue up from the temples at the foot of Núi Sam.
heroCaption: A pavilion on the slope of Núi Sam, with the delta plain behind it

notice.title: This is a climb
notice.body: The shrine and Tây An are at the foot. Chùa Hang is on the slope. Do not treat the cave walk as another flat hall.

body: Continue up from the foot-of-the-hill temples. Vietnam Tourism describes the view from the climb toward Cambodia, and a network of caves in the hillside if there is time. TITC uses the name Phước Điền for this pagoda. The photograph is the pavilion and the plain, which is the view you came up for.

The second frame is the building against the rock, with the path and a statue on the stone. That is the climb, not the shrine at the gate below. A clock for clearer air was not printed. Come when you can see the plain.
A fee and an hour were not on the pages opened. Check on arrival. The cable car TITC mentions for the hill has no published fare either.

figures.caption: The pagoda against the rock, and the path up Núi Sam
figures.alt: Cave Pagoda built into the rock of Sam Mountain, with a white statue in front

gettingThere: Chùa Hang is on the slope of Núi Sam, above the foot-of-the-hill cluster in phường Vĩnh Tế. Start from the shrine road and continue up. Minutes were not printed.

legs.heading: From Ba Chua Xu Temple
legs.body: On foot, up the slope. A published walking time was not found. Check on arrival.

closed: No weekly closing day was published. Check the board on arrival.
admissionNote: No gate tariff was on the pages opened. Check on arrival.
